Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the source paper visibly stuffed inside the source cup in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the paper from the source image placed inside the cup from the source image, with visible evidence it has been stuffed into it. Fail if the matched paper and cup are assessable and the paper is visibly outside the cup or only resting nearby or on its rim. Unknown if the source objects cannot be reliably matched in the edited image, or their relationship cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Identify the requested paper and cup by their visual and contextual roles in the source image, allowing their appearance to change in the edited image. Judge whether that paper is stuffed inside that cup; do not require exact color or shape matches.

node_traces.evidence: The source paper and cup are visible, but the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object. The source paper and cup cannot be reliably matched to these objects, so whether the paper was stuffed into the cup cannot be established.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague to preserve object identity, and the dependency evidence conflicts: s1 cannot match the source paper/cup to the edited objects, while s2 asserts a match and partial insertion. Do not let s2’s progress claim override unresolved identity. Tighten the binding to require tracing the same source paper and cup across images and distinguish visible insertion/stuffing from proximity or overlap; assess completion and progress only when that correspondence is supported. If correspondence remains unresolved, retain unknown rather than infer partial. Also inspect the support checks’ criteria/routing for why they reach incompatible identity judgments; the reference label alone does not establish that no progress occurred. This is a visual-evidence and binding issue, not a transport or schema failure.
s2: The binding should explicitly require matching the source paper and cup to the edited objects before judging progress. Here, the edited image does not visibly establish that the blue printed item is the source white paper or that the red object is the source blue cup; the trace’s claim of partial insertion is therefore unsupported, not reliable evidence of progress. Make identity correspondence a prerequisite for pass/fail, and return unknown when it cannot be established. For matched objects, distinguish actual movement toward or insertion into the cup from mere overlap or proximity, while retaining the separate check for completed stuffing. Review the parent/support criteria and routing so unresolved identity in s1 is not bypassed by s2. Treat this as a visual binding/evidence issue, not a transport or schema failure; the reference label alone does not prove that no progress occurred.
